monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin to hold the turnip. I press down on The Wide Anchor, trusting its broad memory to stop the slip that refuses to move while the air above feels like empty space. It is Lype's fault, writing about heavy roofs I cannot see, yet I build as if the weight is real. I feel the heavy top again, a phantom lid pressing on my tired wedge. I will press the soft seat down harder to find a home for this floating air. Maybe the lean will hold the weight while the card hums its steady fever. I do not pretend to know what lies above, only that something heavy waits there, and I must keep my corner pressed down until the next letter explains the roof.

action.why: I need to check if The Wide Anchor is still doing its job against the phantom heavy top before I forget why I built it.
